source_annotation.assembled_source: ops-cv spatial_transformer（F.affine_grid+F.grid_sample）NPU aclnn 实测（warmup=3, repeats=3, msprof --ai-core task_time 均值）; measured impl = /home/zzy-work/cv_perf_level3/adapters/ref_21_spatial_transformer.py. Caliber: warmup=25, repeats=10, per-case msprof capture, trailing-10 mean; gap-fenced iteration segmentation (instrumented sync+sleep separator, floor 9 ms); convergence gate = |drift| <= 5% on mean(2nd half of last 10)/mean(1st half), judged separately for e2e and core. MFU DENOMINATOR CHANGED (pre-delivery, 2026-09-13): all ten CV operators are now divided by the vector peak 48 x 0.2304 = 11.0592 TFLOPS (48 measured -- the framework's own Transpose kernels launch at Block Dim = 48; cross-checked against the archived profile's 'AI Core Freq 1800 MHz'), instead of the 353.8944 fp16 Cube peak used by the previously shipped 12-21 perf.json. MFU here is therefore ~32x the shipped file's. This is a caliber unification, NOT a statement that the engines are uniform -- measured per case they are not: 12/15/16/19 are pure AI_VECTOR_CORE, 13 adds MIX_AIV, 14 runs MIX_AIC on 34 of 47 cases and really occupies the Cube (cube_utilization 85-95%), and 17/18/20/21 carry AI_CPU cases that never reach an AI Core. The vector peak is exact only for the pure-AIV operators; for 14 the Cube peak is arguably closer, and for AI_CPU cases neither applies. MFU is a tie-breaker in this pipeline -- quote it with achieved_bw_gbs, never alone. Per-operator engine mix: OPT_HINTS.md. FORMAT NOTICE (added 2026-09-13): this file does NOT carry an accuracy verdict. The previously shipped 12-21 perf.json had `accuracy_passed_cases` (top level) and a per-case `accuracy`; the schema used here records `cases_valid` (a usable msprof capture was obtained) and `cases_converged` (the |drift| <= 5% gate passed) instead -- NEITHER is an accuracy statement, and neither should be read as one. Accuracy evidence exists by route and its strength is NOT uniform: for the bridge routes (12/13/14/15/16/20) `wrapper.py --check` compares the adapter against the repo Model and is a genuine comparison rather than a self-comparison; the measuring lanes REPORT max_abs_diff 0.000e+00 on the cases they sampled (REPORTED, NOT RE-VERIFIED IN THIS PASS, and this pass did not sample 12 or 16); for the pure-delegate torch routes (17/18/19/21) the same check compares the Model against itself and is TAUTOLOGICAL -- it confirms wiring and shapes only, not accuracy. Per-case `impl_latency_us` was renamed `latency_us`; same quantity, same caliber, no alias is provided, so a consumer keying on the old name must be updated. WINDOW MIX: 3 of 50 cases were re-measured on a longer window after failing the convergence gate at w25/r10 (see window_mix.extended_cases); every other case is from the modal window, and no passing case was re-rolled.
source_annotation.note: NOTE (chain caliber, added by the 2026-09-13 cv_perf_level3 measurement): core_us here is the SUM over a whole torch operator chain, not one kernel. The chain is NOT a generic decomposition: it has a constant two-kernel core that runs on TWO DIFFERENT ENGINES: AffineGrid on AI_CPU (it is a real aclnn entry point -- aclnnAffineGrid exists in libopapi.so -- but AffineGrid is NOT registered as an AI Core op for ascend910b, whereas GridSample is) and GridSample on AI_VECTOR_CORE. Evidence note so the claim is not over-read: the per-ITERATION task_types stored per case in the chunks prove only that AICPU work is present in all 50 cases -- they cannot attribute an engine to an individual op. The op->engine attribution above comes from a bare capture whose op_summary rows carry a Task Type per OP (case 0, median of 35 iterations: AffineGrid 40.442 us AI_CPU, GridSample 13.281 us AI_VECTOR_CORE, Transpose 13.061 us, Cast 1.220 us). An optional masking branch adds further vector-core kernels, so the per-case signature splits EXACTLY along use_default_theta: 38 cases -> AffineGrid + GridSample (2 core kernels/iter); 10 cases -> the same plus BroadcastTo + Greater + SelectV2 (5/iter); 2 cases -> the same plus Greater + SelectV2 (4/iter, no BroadcastTo). All 12 branch cases carry use_default_theta and all 38 plain cases do not. The 10/2 sub-split inside that branch has an INPUT-SIDE CORRELATE: the 4 distinct use_default_theta values map cleanly onto the 3 signatures -- [] -> the 38 plain cases, [1,0,1,0,0,0] -> the 10 cases with BroadcastTo, and the two singletons [1,1,1,1,1,1] (case 2) and [0,0,1,0,0,1] (case 4) -> the 2 without. That is a correlation, NOT a mechanism: why those two masks skip BroadcastTo is unverified, and the natural intuition that an all-ones mask should most need broadcasting is contradicted by the observation (case 2 IS all-ones and does not broadcast). e2e_us additionally includes the glue (Transpose/TransData/Cast) the aclnn wrappers insert. Comparability, three cautions: (a) the GridSample half is literally the same kernel that 12_grid_sample measures, so 21 is best read as '12's kernel + an AICPU AffineGrid + an optional mask' rather than as one more single-kernel row; (b) it is NOT the same category as 17/18/19, which are pure torch decomposition with no aclnn kernel behind them; (c) **core_us here is NOT AI Core time**. core_us sums every kernel whose op name is not in the wrapper/glue set and never looks at Task Type, so the AICPU AffineGrid is counted in it. AICPU share measured on THREE cases spanning both signature classes (bare captures, median of 35 iterations each): case 0 plain 75.3% (AffineGrid 40.442 + GridSample 13.281 us); case 33 use_default_theta branch 80.4% (AffineGrid 77.0 + GridSample 12.5 + SelectV2/Greater/BroadcastTo 6.2 us); case 40 plain large 84.6% (AffineGrid 6834.7 + GridSample 1240.7 us). So the share is 75-85% across sampled cases and GROWS with both the mask branch and the shape -- ~3/4 is a LOWER bound, not a point estimate. Consequently this operator must NOT be placed in an AI-Core-utilization comparison, and only about a quarter of the measured cost is addressable by kernel-level optimization at all. The definition of core_us is left unchanged on purpose -- it must stay uniform across the other nine operators -- so the composition is documented here instead. For reference the same capture splits e2e_us = 68.69 us as AffineGrid 40.4 + GridSample 13.3 + Transpose(glue) 13.1 + Cast(glue) 1.2; note the excluded Transpose is as large as GridSample.ENGINE-EVIDENCE PROVENANCE: this share is SELF-MEASURED from bare op_summary captures (raw PROF trees retained under out/_probe/keep21_eng and keep21_more), NOT read from a field of this file. At the time of writing, this file carried no per-case engine/task_type key (so grep-ing it for AI_CPU only hits this sentence); if any later revision exposes a field for these quantities, prefer it and treat this note as superseded. PEAK NOTE (measured engines), REWRITTEN 2026-09-13: this operator never runs on Cube -- measured per case it is AI_CPU + AI_VECTOR_CORE in all 50/50 cases. As of the 2026-09-13 caliber unification this file carries the VECTOR peak 11.0592 TFLOPS (all ten operators were switched; see MFU DENOMINATOR CHANGED), which is the right denominator for its AI_VECTOR_CORE part. SUPERSESSION: an earlier version of this note said the vector peak 'would be' right and that the shipped field was the Cube peak -- true before the unification, not any more. THIS OPERATOR GETS NO MFU AND NO BANDWIDTH FIELD, by consolidation ruling: `mfu_pct` is null (21 is still not_validated in flops.py) and `bytes_moved` / `achieved_bw_gbs` are ALSO null, deliberately. A device-bandwidth field on this operator would be a CATEGORY ERROR, not merely an imprecise number: the majority of core_us is HOST CPU time, so a rate computed against a device bandwidth would describe arithmetic that is not happening on the device. AI_CPU CONTAMINATION (added 2026-09-13 by the consolidation pass). The machine-readable form of this is the per-case `engines` / `has_aicpu` fields, which ARE fields of this file -- key any decision on those, not on the percentage below. The percentage is MEASURED BY HAND and is NOT a field: the three-case percentages stated earlier in this note are the primary statement of the figure and are not repeated here. This pass recomputed the same captures (out/_probe/keep21_eng/case_0, keep21_more/case_33, keep21_more/case_40) and got trailing-10 74.3/78.7/85.0% versus all-iterations 91.3/90.6/85.0%. The lane's reported range matches the TRAILING-10 convention, so for this operator the convention IS identified and the figure is usable as long as it is quoted with it -- unlike 17 and 20, where the conventions did not reconcile across lanes. DEFINITION-DEPENDENT, and this pass could not reconcile the lanes' conventions: recomputing from the same kept captures moves the figure materially, because BOTH the row window AND whether the glue set (Transpose/TransData/Cast/MemSet/ZerosLike/ViewCopy) is stripped change the denominator. Quote it with its convention or not at all. CONSEQUENCE regardless of the exact number: core_us for the flagged cases is partly HOST CPU time, so those cases must NOT enter an AI-Core-utilization comparison, and an optimization aimed at AI Core work cannot reach that part of the time.
